title: Migration safety lattice — runtime & control-plane bridge notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing an alternative upgrade choreography we’re calling the "safety lattice" — a set of overlapping, progressively stronger safety gates that let us simultaneously evolve the runtime and control plane with minimal customer disruption in private (VPC / on-prem) deployments.

Audience:
Eng-private-deployments, SRE, Release Eng, Solutions Eng, and any SEs running customer cutovers.

High-level goals:
- Zero or minimal traffic errors (API contract preserved) for pinned clients.
- Fast rollback paths with state reconciliation hooks.
- Minimal owner intervention for most migrations (automation + clear playbooks).
- Terraform-friendly: allow module-by-module rollout with clear state migration steps.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Customers may be air-gapped, use local KMS/HSM, and run older appliance images.
- Some customers pin runtime versions and disable automatic model updates.
- Network topology diversity (private subnets, NAT gateways, internal proxies) — expect varying egress capabilities.
- On-prem hardware heterogeneity: GPUs and CPU-only fallback nodes possible.

Scope of this doc:
- Runtime binary upgrade (+kv cache metadata migration), control-plane (agents/agent-proxy) compatibility shim, API contract adapters, Terraform state changes and rollbacks.
- NOT covering: billing/usage migration, customer data model changes at storage level (separate plan).

Safety lattice overview (concept):
- Gate 0 — Dry-run verification: artifact signatures, hash checks, config syntax checks.
- Gate 1 — Probe-only rollout: deploy side-by-side in lab/edge with no production traffic. Automated smoke tests run and produce signal.
- Gate 2 — Canary with shadowed traffic: route live traffic to new runtime in shadow mode to compare outputs and perf. No client-visible path.
- Gate 3 — Canary with %-traffic on non-critical routes: small slices, multi-tenant isolation where possible.
- Gate 4 — Regional opt-in ramp: allow region/customer to opt-in to new control-plane features.
- Gate 5 — Full flip with automatic KV migration & final reconciliation.

Pre-upgrade checklist (quick):
- [ ] Backup control-plane state (etcd/s3 snapshots depending on deployment).
- [ ] Terraform state exported and locked. Document current module versions.
- [ ] Customer certs/keys validity check; prepare rotation plan.
- [ ] All api clients list: who pins model/runtime? create contact list.
- [ ] Define SLO leakage threshold for the migration (e.g., 0.5% elevated 5xx allowed for 30min window).

Terraform module notes (what we changed / keep in mind):
- Keep module interfaces backward compatible; avoid renaming top-level resources.
- Introduce new resource blocks behind feature flags (var.enable_runtime_bridge = false by default).
- For stateful resources (e.g., kv-store, onprem-cache-volume) provide migration helpers: separate tf resource that performs snapshot -> import steps rather than in-place replacement.
- Avoid implicit replacement of appliance nodes. If a node image must change, use a blue/green pattern: create new node pool, warm it, then drain old.
- Sample TF pattern we used: create resource redwood_runtime_bridge (count = var.enable_runtime_bridge ? 1 : 0) so we can toggle without resource renames.

Runtime & KV cache migration considerations:
- KV layout: old runtime stores prefix metadata v1; new runtime expects v2 with expiration encoding. Provide a compatibility shim that reads v1 and generates v2 lazily on access.
- Bulk migration only at Gate 5 with throttled background workers; during early gates rely on lazy conversion to avoid write spikes.
- Preserve eviction policies — test with synthetic TTLs in lab.
- Ensure prefix-key hashing unchanged or provide mapping table. If hash changes, we must run a pre-cutover mapping job that creates alias pointers for legacy keys.

Control-plane compatibility shim strategy:
- Provide a shim component (controlplane-compat-proxy) that translates legacy agent heartbeats and API versions to the new control-plane format.
- Shim runs in parallel; expose metrics for conversion failures. If failures exceed threshold, automatically rollback agent upgrade.
- Agents should be upgradeable in two phases: agent binary upgrade (with legacy flag), then enable new heartbeat schema.

API contract & client compatibility:
- Contract-first: maintain shape of public endpoints; extend with new headers instead of changing response shapes.
- Where header-based negotiation is used, default to legacy behavior unless client declares support (via X-Runtime-Version or similar).
- For streaming endpoints, maintain previous chunk framing. If we must change framing, provide a shim that re-frames for legacy clients.

Traffic shifting patterns and safe rollbacks:
- Use percentage ramp with cookie-affinity for client pinning (so we can target specific customers).
- Maintain automatic fallback policy: if 5xx rate for new variant > threshold for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows, flip traffic back and quarantine nodes.
- Rollback checklist (fast path):
  1) Pause new deployment autoscaler; set TF feature flag to false to prevent future instances.
  2) Re-route traffic to last-known-good control-plane endpoint via routing policy (regional DNS or local LB change).
  3) Rehydrate KV aliases/shims to re-enable legacy reads if necessary.
  4) Revert Terraform state with a previously saved state file (doc saved at pre-upgrade step).

Verification & metrics to watch (SLO-oriented):
- API 5xx and 4xx (client/contract) rates per route.
- p50/p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints.
- Output-drift metric for shadowed requests (semantic diff count / token-level diff heuristics).
- KV conversion failure rate and TTL skew.
- Agent heartbeat jitter and reconciliation latency.

Playbook for a single customer cutover (abbreviated):
- Phase A — Lab rehearsal (T-14 to T-3 days): full deployment in lab mirrored to customer infra config. Run smoke suite and perf harness. Document deltas.
- Phase B — Shadow canary (T-2 days): enable Gate 2, run 24–72h, collect output-drift and perf. Post-mortem any anomalies.
- Phase C — Small percentage release (T-1 day): pick non-critical tenant routes, 1–5% traffic, sampling. Keep old and new for quick switch.
- Phase D — Regional opt-in (T+0): selected customers migrate, enable background KV migration workers with throttling.
- Phase E — Full flip (T+1 to T+7): monitor, increase traffic, finalize state reconciliation, deprecate shim after 30 days.

Operator runbook — checklist (short commands & references):
- Snapshot control plane: etcdctl snapshot save /backups/etcd-$(date +%s).db
- Export terraform state: terraform state pull > pre-upgrade-state-YYYYMMDD.json
- Start bridge components: kubectl apply -f controlplane-compat-deploy.yaml --record
- Start KV migrator (throttled): ./kv-migrator --rate=200 --batch=500 --dry-run=false
- Healthcheck: curl -sS -H "X-Run-Version: probe" https://local-controlplane/health | jq '.'

Open questions / unresolved risks (callouts):
- Air-gapped installs: how do we deliver signed artifacts if customer restricts external downloads? Need documented S3 staging + artifact-signing flow. (See INF-8421).
- KMS integration: rotated keys might block agent re-registration; we need a pre-cutover key-check script.
- Terraform state drift: customers with manual changes will complicate automated blue/green; recommend a pre-cutover manual tf import sweep.

Appendix — test snippets and useful queries:
- List agent versions and last heartbeat:
  kubectl get pods -l app=redwood-agent -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.metadata.labels.version} {.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].lastTransitionTime}\n'

- Simple output-drift comparator (local):
  python tools/output_diff.py --baseline baseline.json --candidate candidate.json --threshold 0.02

- Terraform toggle example (pattern):
  variable "enable_runtime_bridge" { type = bool default = false }
  resource "redwood_runtime_bridge" "bridge" {
    count = var.enable_runtime_bridge ? 1 : 0
    image = var.bridge_image
  }
Post-upgrade cleanup notes:
- Keep controlplane-compat-proxy running for at least 30 days to catch late clients; promote conversion logs to long-retention if errors seen.
- Rotate ephemeral certs only after verifying agent stability for 72 hours.
- Archive pre-upgrade terraform state with encryption and store reference in the ticket.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft customer-ready one-pager that lists exact rollback button steps for Solutions Eng (action item Ethan).
- Wire up a dashboard panel for "shadow drift rate" in the Console. (Marta).
- Add a terraform module doc for the migrate-import helper and include example commands for importing existing volumes. (Connor).

End of draft — this is intentionally conversational and contains TODOs. Use as the canonical working place for the safety-lattice choreography until we convert to a formal playbook.
